purpose: Track where the public-source literature is thin and consented oral/practitioner testimony will eventually be needed.

debts.area: smell of dying and deathcare rooms
debts.why_it_matters: The seed flags smell as rarely written and widely known to practitioners; public sources are sparse and clinically skewed.
Families often remember oxygen concentrators, pumps, doorbells, phones, and equipment removal; public sources rarely preserve their felt texture.

debts.area: body weight and tactile after-death knowledge
debts.why_it_matters: The seed names the body’s specific weight after death as knowledge held by nurses and morticians; public rendering is risky.

debts.area: child sensory memories of death rooms
debts.why_it_matters: Children’s sensory memories may be powerful but are highest-risk and likely often private.

debts.area: pets and animal companions at deathbeds
debts.why_it_matters: The seed flags animals as underdocumented and widely observed; public therapy-animal sources do not cover own-pet bedside phenomenology well.
